name: Oak Savanna and Cactus Loop Trail
governance: The Nature Conservancy
description: This trail passes through one of the finest examples in Ohio of globally rare black oak savanna and Midwest sand barrens. Hikers will cross over 15,000 year-old sand dunes and observe plants such as prickly pear cactus, wild blue lupine and grass pink and orange fringed orchids.
identity_notes: Trail at Kitty Todd Nature Preserve (TNC). Parking at 10420 Old State Line Road.

name: Salamander Flats Wetland Trail
governance: The Nature Conservancy
accessibility: Mowed grass on firm sandy soil with occasional low areas of standing water or saturated soil in spring/winter; tread width 3 ft; grade less than 5%; cross slope less than 2%
description: Hikers can observe globally rare mesic sand prairie, previously an agricultural field restored by The Nature Conservancy. In the spring, thousands of the rare twisted yellow-eyed grass bloom along the trail bed in shallow vernal pools. These pools also provide breeding habitat for spring peppers, chorus frogs and salamanders.
identity_notes: Trail at Kitty Todd Nature Preserve (TNC). Length: 0.75 mile round trip. Separate trailhead/parking from main preserve entrance.
